From: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx spikes and high tail latency (prod)

I've started a log/trace sweep across the serving runtime. Initial hypothesis: a client-side integration (StreamSoft proxy) appears to be sending partial chunked responses or dropping chunk boundaries when request-response timing crosses a threshold — our streaming parser in the client SDK tolerates well-formed chunked encodings but exhibits edge-case failures when the final chunk/trailer arrives on a delayed packet.

Specific observations so far:
- Multiple internal traces show: 200 OK + chunked body where the last chunk and HTTP trailers arrive in a separate TCP segment that the client proxy drops/combines incorrectly.
- When that happens, our SDK streaming parser returns EOF mid-body which client code treats as an application error, leading to retries and amplified downstream load.
- A small percentage of requests (0.5-1%) are affected, but they cluster during high-concurrency bursts which matches NorthStar's incident window.

Ask to NorthStar: please provide the pcap fragment for one failing event and confirm the exact SDK version + any TLS termination or keepalive timeouts in StreamSoft. Also, StreamSoft, if you're on this thread, can you share proxy config (buffering, max header size, allowed chunk extensions)?

I'll start drafting a mitigation: 1) a short-term compatibility shim in the SDK to be more tolerant of split trailers, 2) a targeted canary patch to the runtime to ensure we don't prematurely close connections, 3) alerting to detect repeat pattern and auto-fallback to non-streaming response for that client.

— Rishi
Senior Engineeer, Serving Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx spikes and high tail latency (prod)

Team — attaching the pcap we captured (pcap_fragment_dump.tar.gz). We run StreamSoft as an edge proxy that performs TLS termination and then forwards to Redwood. Config notes:
- StreamSoft version: 3.5.1-custom
- Keepalive idle: 45s, max header size: 64KB, buffering: on for requests > 8KB
- We do opportunistic connection pooling across multiple upstreams (we were on two Redwood endpoints during the spike).

I marked a failing request in the pcap. We observed that the server sent the final chunk and HTTP trailers in a subsequent TCP packet; StreamSoft forwarded the packets but in a few samples it appears to coalesce and drop the empty final-chunk marker, resulting in a truncated body at the client. Attaching the pcap.

-- NS SRE

Attached: pcap_fragment_dump.tar.gz

Date: 2027-04-02T09:03:00Z
Subject: URGENT exec brief: NorthStar production impact — proposed next steps

Laura / Connor — loop you both in with an exec summary. TL;DR: NorthStar (NS-9871) is seeing intermittent client-observed truncation on streaming responses which is causing retries and downstream 5xx spikes. Root appears to be interaction between our streaming parser behavior and StreamSoft's custom proxy behavior when the final chunk/trailer is split onto a late TCP packet. Rishi has a proposed mitigations list.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Approve an emergency SDK compatibility patch (compat-shim) to tolerate split trailers and avoid returning EOF mid-body. Patch window: 48–72 hours to verification and canary.
2) If needed, deploy a short runtime guard to detect sequence pattern and fall back to non-streaming responses for affected client IPs for up to 24 hours.
3) Offer NorthStar a goodwill credit per the SLA for measured impact (Marissa, please propose matrix).

Attachments: proposed_hotfix_patch_notes.md, SLA_credit_matrix.xlsx, JIRA-INF-7623 link.

Requesting a quick decision so Eng can start the branch.

— Sean
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
